payload.title: How to Get Married in Hawaii Step by Step
payload.excerpt: Hawaii is on your list, and before you fall for a lawn above the Pacific you want to know two things: will the marriage be legal, and what do you do first? Getting married in Hawaii as an Australian couple is straightforward.
key_takeaways: Australians can marry legally in Hawaii by following the Hawaii State Department of Health marriage licence process, with no residency requirement.
You both meet a licence agent in person no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony, and the wedding must take place within 30 days of picking up the licence.
Your officiant must hold a State of Hawaii performer licence, whoever they are and wherever they come from.
Order certified copies of your marriage certificate early, because a certified copy is usually accepted as proof of the marriage back in Australia.

faq.q: Who needs to be at the ceremony?
faq.a: The licence steps centre on the two of you, your licence agent and a state-licensed officiant. Ask your officiant what the ceremony itself requires on the day, including witnesses, and how the marriage is registered afterwards.

faq.q: Can a friend from Australia officiate our wedding in Hawaii?
faq.a: Yes, if they hold a State of Hawaii performer licence. Every officiant must be licensed by the State of Hawaii Department of Health before performing a marriage, and performers register online at marriage.ehawaii.gov.

faq.q: How far ahead can we get our Hawaii marriage licence?
faq.a: You can complete the online application before you travel, but you meet the agent no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony. The ceremony must then take place within 30 days of pick-up, or the licence is void.

faq.q: Is a Hawaii marriage recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is legally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it in Australia, and your Hawaii certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage.

faq.q: Do we need a permit to marry on a Hawaii beach?
faq.a: On unencumbered State shoreline, yes: a right-of-entry permit through DLNR's Wiki Permits system, with a Certificate of Liability Insurance. A few beaches are managed by other agencies, such as the counties, and they authorise those instead.

faq.q: Can we have a symbolic ceremony in Hawaii and marry legally at home?
faq.a: Yes. A symbolic ceremony is not a legal marriage, so the Hawaii licence applies only if you want the ceremony to be legally binding. If you marry legally in Hawaii instead, you cannot marry again in Australia, though you can hold a recommitment ceremony.
